summary: At segment 0 step 61, input newline reaches trap.c:chest_trap() through #loot on a trapped floor chest. C prints “You trigger a trap!” and explicitly displays WIN_MESSAGE before the first Luck/rn2 check, producing a --More-- boundary (cursor [27,0,1]); JavaScript writes the same message but omits the explicit message-window display, leaving the cursor at [62,0,1]. The first screen difference is the missing --More-- marker; RNG values match for the full recording. The source-aligned fix belongs immediately after ttyPline() in js/trap.js:chest_trap(), using its existing displayPendingTtyMessageWindow import before any chest-trap RNG.

dependencies: C win/tty/wintty.c:tty_display_nhwindow(WIN_MESSAGE,FALSE) is represented by the already imported js/tty_message.js:displayPendingTtyMessageWindow(state). ttyPline() records the pending top line with TOPLINE_NEED_MORE; the explicit display call consumes that pending message boundary. In js/trap.js:chest_trap(), the existing comment incorrectly treats ttyPline() alone as equivalent.

chest_trap() returns whether the chest was destroyed, but all three C caller sites discard that result (including explicit (void) casts in pickup.c and trap.c). No return-valued C callee needs to be added for this display-boundary correction.
